summary: getUser now reads the user id from a destructured route param, puts the id in its 404 message, and adds a fetchedAt timestamp to the response.

findings.title: Handler reads a route param that does not exist
findings.problem: getUser reads req.params.userId. The route in src/routes/users.js:7 declares the param as :id, so userId is always undefined.
findings.consequence: findUser(undefined) returns nothing, so every GET /users/:id call gets a 404. The 404 message also reads 'no user with id undefined'.
findings.fix: Read the id param that the route defines. Renaming the route param to :userId would also work.
findings.suggested_change:
const { id: userId } = req.params;
  const user = findUser(userId);

findings.title: No test covers the changed getUser behaviour
findings.problem: This change alters how getUser reads its param and what it returns. The repository has no test that exercises getUser.
findings.consequence: A test calling the route would have caught the broken param lookup. Without one, future regressions in this handler will also go unnoticed.
findings.fix: Add a test that requests GET /users/1 and checks for a 200 status with a fetchedAt field. Add a second test that checks the 404 for an unknown id.
